Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a and 1b) shows a well-defined, smooth, round radiopaque mass located in the lower trachea (indicated by arrows), which is characteristic of a tracheal hamartoma. Malignancies typically present with irregular or spiculated margins, while foreign bodies usually have distinct shapes like coins or batteries, and stenosis would show narrowing without a discrete mass.
